dimensions.presentCompetition: Chinese domestic supply chain ➔ Domestic priority with strict export controls (LFP battery chemistry, smart cockpits, ADAS neural networks).

dimensions.pastCooperation: European OEMs commanded board majorities, brand licensing authority, and dividend distributions through technological superiority.
dimensions.presentCompetition: Chinese partners dominate software and battery supply chains, reducing Western OEMs to technological licensees.

dimensions.pastCooperation: Domestic production was strictly earmarked for mainland sales; global exports were controlled by Western headquarters.
dimensions.presentCompetition: Mega-fabs in China (BMW Shenyang iX3, Tesla Shanghai, Volvo Chengdu) increasingly re-export finished vehicles into Europe.

dimensions.pastCooperation: Mandatory 50:50 JV rules and technology sharing under Foreign Investment Guidance Catalogs.
dimensions.presentCompetition: PRC Export Control Law, Data Security Law, and Anti-Espionage statutes statutorily prohibit outbound repatriation of advanced IP.

domainSpecificEvidence.europeStatus: European OEMs maintain strong structural engineering, high-strength steel-aluminum bonding, and NVH acoustic tuning leadership.
domainSpecificEvidence.chinaStatus: Pioneered integrated high-pressure Giga-Casting, reducing manufacturing unit costs by 30% and drastically simplifying structural assembly.
domainSpecificEvidence.flowDirection: While China leads in rapid structural casting innovation, Europe retains leverage in premium chassis dynamics and crash safety.

domainSpecificEvidence.europeStatus: European gigafactory initiatives face delays (e.g., Northvolt financial restructuring), resulting in persistent reliance on imported cells.
domainSpecificEvidence.chinaStatus: CATL and BYD control over 85% of global LFP manufacturing and hold near-monopoly positions in mineral refining (Lithium 65%, Graphite 90%).
domainSpecificEvidence.flowDirection: German Triad EV production is structurally dependent on Chinese battery suppliers and mainland cell capacity.

domainSpecificEvidence.europeStatus: In-house software restructuring at CARIAD (>€6B cumulative losses) caused vehicle launch delays across premium platforms.
domainSpecificEvidence.chinaStatus: XPENG centralized CEA zonal E/E architecture and Huawei HarmonyOS smart cockpits set regional benchmarks for software-defined vehicles.
domainSpecificEvidence.flowDirection: Volkswagen committed $705M to acquire an equity stake and license XPENG CEA architecture, reversing historical software directionality.

domainSpecificEvidence.europeStatus: GDPR compliance and privacy regulations constrain large-scale video ingestion for end-to-end AI training.
domainSpecificEvidence.chinaStatus: Over 10 million connected vehicles harvest real-world telemetry daily; Data Security Law statutorily bans outbound cross-border transfer.
domainSpecificEvidence.flowDirection: Mainland driving data cannot be transferred to European headquarters, necessitating bifurcated, isolated localized training clusters.

domainSpecificEvidence.europeStatus: Siemens industrial automation, programmable logic controllers (PLCs), and precision machinery remain global leaders.
domainSpecificEvidence.chinaStatus: Following Midea's 2016 acquisition of KUKA, robotics IP and automated assembly systems were integrated into domestic battery and EV lines.
domainSpecificEvidence.flowDirection: Core robotics hardware IP was absorbed by Chinese capital, though European systems integrators retain process optimization know-how.
